brief.topic: Where to put human approval gates in an agent
brief.audience: PMs and engineers designing agent workflows

coreInsight: Put approval gates on actions, not on the whole agent: the harder an action is to undo, the earlier a human approves it.

hooks.text: Don’t approve the agent. Approve the action.
hooks.notes: Shifts the debate from trusting the agent to gating specific actions.

hooks.text: Your agent needs four gate levels, not one.
hooks.notes: Concrete but sounds like a list.

hooks.text: Approving every agent step defeats the point.
hooks.notes: True, but doesn’t say where gates go.

selectionRationale: Highest total (23/25): a crisp reframe that the gate map makes concrete and the refund example proves.

caption.opening: “Human in the loop” for an agent shouldn’t mean approving every step. Gate the actions instead.
body:
A simple gate map:
→ Read-only lookups: no gate, just log them
→ Drafts and internal notes: spot-check later
→ Messages to customers: approve before sending
→ Money, deletes, permissions: always approve
The rule: the harder an action is to undo, the earlier a human steps in. List every tool your agent can call and give each one a gate level before launch.
